english.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken choice when an event is expected soon or is nearly happening.
This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something will happen very soon.
Use this when nearly means that an event or change is about to happen soon.
Use this when the event is imminent or very soon to happen.
Use this when “nearly” means that something is imminent or will happen soon.
Use this when something is almost about to happen or a time or stage is imminent.

examples.english: Hurry up, the bus will arrive momentarily.
examples.traditional: 快啲啦，架巴士就快到喇。
